title: Tame descent of prime-degree towers and the immediate obstruction criterion
statement: All fields below are fields [def-weil-field] with compatible nontrivial nonarchimedean real absolute values. For such a field $A$, write $A^\circ=\{x:|x|\le1\}$ for its valuation ring [def-trf-valuation-ring], $\widetilde A=A^\circ/\{x:|x|<1\}$ and $\Gamma_A=|A^\times|$. For a finite extension $B/A$ set $e(B/A)=[\Gamma_B:\Gamma_A]$, $f(B/A)=[\widetilde B:\widetilde A]$ and $d(B/A)=[B:A]/(e(B/A)f(B/A))$. Call it immediate if its value group and residue field equal those of $A$, unramified if $e=d=1$ and the residue extension is separable, and tame if $d=1$, its residue extension is separable and its ramification index is prime to the residue characteristic (with no index restriction in residue characteristic zero). A field extension is separable if every algebraic element has a minimal polynomial with distinct roots. Let $A$ be complete and let $p=\operatorname{char}(\widetilde A)>0$. (1) If $B/A$ is finite of degree a power of $p$, there is a finite tame extension $A^\prime/A$ in a common algebraic closure such that $BA^\prime/A^\prime$ admits a finite tower whose nonidentity successive degrees are all $p$. (2) If no finite extension $B/A$ admits a finite immediate extension of degree $p$, then every finite extension $C/A$ has $d(C/A)=1$.

source.place: §2.1, p. 9 (maximal tame extension has pro-p absolute Galois group); §6.1 opening, p. 36 (criterion); proof of Theorem 6.3.1, first paragraph, p. 49 (finite tame descent and prime-degree towers).

proof.text: Fix the algebraic closure $\Omega$ and its extending absolute value. By [lem-trf-maximal-tame-galois-p-property], the field $T$, the union of finite tame extensions of $A$ in $\Omega$, is algebraic over $A$ and every finite Galois extension of $T$ has $p$-power degree. The characteristic of $T$ is $0$ or $p$, since a field with residue characteristic $p$ has characteristic $0$ or $p$. For ANY finite $D/A$, the extension $DT/T$ is finite. Apply [lem-trf-galois-p-property-prime-towers] to obtain a degree-$p$ tower from $T$ to $DT$, including when $D/A$ is inseparable.

source.place: Section 2.1, printed p. 9; proof of Theorem 6.3.1, first paragraph, printed p. 49.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-algebraic-union-finite-tower-descent] to this tower with $M=T$, $B=D$. It gives a finite $A^\prime\subseteq T$ and a tower from $A^\prime$ to $DA^\prime$ with the same successive degrees $p$. By [lem-trf-maximal-tame-galois-p-property], $A^\prime/A$ is tame. With $D=B$ this proves (1); in fact the construction works without the $p$-power restriction on $[B:A]$. If the tower is empty, the descent statement gives $DA^\prime=A^\prime$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 6.3.1, first paragraph, printed p. 49, finite tame descent.

proof.text: Assume the hypothesis of (2), and suppose for contradiction that some finite $C/A$ has $d(C/A)>1$. Apply the construction of steps 1--2 with $D=C$. By [lem-trf-valued-finite-ramification-calculus], $CA^\prime/C$ is tame (base change of $A^\prime/A$), all the fields in the resulting finite tower are complete, and multiplicativity gives $$d(CA^\prime/A^\prime)=\frac{d(CA^\prime/C)d(C/A)}{d(A^\prime/A)}=d(C/A)>1.$$ Thus one of its degree-$p$ steps $E_{i+1}/E_i$ has defect greater than one, since the product of their defects is greater than one.

source.place: Corollary 6.1.6 proof, printed p. 41; Section 2.1, printed p. 9.

proof.text: For that step write $e=e(E_{i+1}/E_i)$, $f=f(E_{i+1}/E_i)$ and $d=d(E_{i+1}/E_i)$. The calculus [lem-trf-valued-finite-ramification-calculus] gives positive integers $e,f$, and $d$ a power of $p$, with $p=efd$. Since $d>1$, this forces $d=p$ and $e=f=1$. Hence $E_{i+1}/E_i$ is an immediate extension of degree $p$, whereas $E_i/A$ is finite. This contradicts the hypothesis of (2). Every finite extension therefore has $d=1$.

source.place: Section 6.1 opening, printed p. 36; Corollary 6.1.6 proof, printed p. 41.
